title: external-pt-evidence-handoff-and-siem-export-runbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This runbook describes the operational steps, export schemas, and evidence-handling patterns we will use when coordinating external penetration tests that require access to RBAC v2 audits, application audit logs, and SIEM exports. It is intended for the security engineering lead (owner), on-call SRE, and the designated solutions engineer who interfaces with the vendor.

Why a separate runbook:
- External engagements frequently require reproducible evidence bundles and a clear chain of custody.
- We want minimal blast radius: ephemeral access, readonly exports, and automated verification.
- The runbook unifies RBAC validation queries, audit-log field mappings, SIEM export formats, and remediation verification steps so reviewers have a single source of truth.

High-level timeline (example engagement):
- Week -2: Scoping call with vendor. Confirm target assets, exclusions, blackout windows.
- Week -1: Prepare evidence buckets, SIEM export config, ephemeral principals. Verify RBAC test accounts.
- Day 0: Kickoff. Provide read-only evidence URLs and the test account.
- Day 0-3: Active testing window (example). Monitor telemetry, rate-limit, and alerts.
- Day 1-5: Daily short sync / triage. Severity 1/TL escalation immediately.
- Day +1 after window: Vendor provides findings. Security team ingests and triages.
- Day +N: Remediation and verification.

Contact & escalation matrix:
- Security owner: Aisha Patel - aisha.patel@redwood.example (primary)
- SRE on-call: pager@redwood.example (rotating)
- Product lead (if API behavior implicated): Marcus Li - marcus.li@redwood.example
- Legal & Compliance: Sofia Alvarez - sofia.alvarez@redwood.example
- Emergency escalation: CTO on-call (Slack #cto-emerg)

Scoping rules / exclusions (must be explicit in scope doc):
- Include: API endpoints in hosted inference control plane, audit logs for control plane actions, RBAC v2 role assignments, SIEM rule sets related to inference runtime alerts, evidence buckets containing request/response logs (sanitized), and relevant cloud IAM audit logs.
- Exclude: Customer PII payloads, private model weights, paywall/billing systems, non-devnet production payment endpoints.
- Sensitive data handling: Any evidence that might contain customer PII must be redacted before upload; if redaction is not possible the vendor must be given a redaction workflow and additional NDA terms.

RBAC v2 validation checklist (pre-run):
- Confirm the test account is mapped to a non-privileged role (role: pen-tester-readonly) that only has read permissions on audit logs and role-assignment endpoints.
- Validate role permissions with the policy-lint tool: policy-lint --role pen-tester-readonly --assert-no-write
- Snapshot role bindings: export-roles --output=roles-snapshot-YYYYMMDD.json. Store checksum (sha256).
- Run a smoke-auth test using the test principal and capture token usage in audit logs.
- Record any existing exceptions/allowlists that would interfere with tests.

Audit log schema mapping (standardized export):
We export audit events as newline-delimited JSON. Each event MUST contain the following canonical fields:
- timestamp (ISO-8601 UTC)
- tenant_id
- user_id (or service_identity)
- principal_type (human|service|system)
- action (string, verb:noun)
- resource_type
- resource_name
- request_id (globally unique)
- session_id
- source_ip
- user_agent
- outcome (success|failure|error)
- result_code (HTTP-ish code or internal code)
- model_name (if inference-related)
- model_version
- tokens_in
- tokens_out
- inference_latency_ms
- kv_cache_hit (boolean)
- storage_object_path (if artifact stored)
- sha256_of_payload (if provided)
- evidence_ref (optional, pointer to S3 object)
Notes: Keep each field present but null if not applicable. Avoid free-form message blobs for critical fields – use structured fields to enable automated analysis.

SIEM export formats and recommended parser behavior:
- Preferred export: compressed ndjson (gzip) with daily roll files named siem-audit-YYYYMMDD.ndjson.gz.
- Field normalization rules: timestamp->@timestamp, tenant_id->tenant.id, user_id->user.id, action->event.action, resource_type->asset.type, source_ip->source.ip, result->event.outcome.
- Parser responsibilities: convert model-specific fields (model_name, tokens_in/out, inference_latency_ms) into numeric fields for dashboards and create a tag event.type:inference.audit when model_name is present.
- Volume considerations: estimate peak event rate for pen tests (we cap exports to 10k events/min to avoid SIEM ingestion overload). Coordinate with SIEM team if tests will exceed that.

Evidence automation and handoff pattern:
Goals: reproducible bundles, minimal manual steps, short-lived access.
Steps to create evidence bundle (automated):
1) Run export job: export-audit --start <start> --end <end> --filter "tags:pen-test" --format ndjson --compress gz --dest s3://redwood-evidence/pt-<engagement-id>/exports/
2) Generate manifests: manifest.json listing filename, sha256, event_count, start_ts, end_ts.
3) Create ephemeral object ACL: put-object-acl --bucket redwood-evidence --prefix pt-<id>/exports/ --acl readonly-signed-url --duration 72h --allowed-ips <vendor-ip list>
4) Create signed access page: evidence-handoff --bucket redwood-evidence --prefix pt-<id> --expire 72h --audit "handed-to:vendor-name" which produces a short URL and a signed token.

Chain-of-custody notes:
- Record when each object is generated and when the signed URL is created (timestamps in manifest).
- Store SHA256 of each file in an immutable evidence index (append-only, write-once storage).
- When vendor downloads, capture HTTP access logs and store as download-audit-<id>.ndjson.gz with IP and user agent.
- Rotate any ephemeral credentials and revoke ACLs immediately after the expiration or when the engagement ends.

SIEM ingestion checklist (pre-engagement):
- Confirm parser for canonical audit fields is deployed and green in staging.
- Verify field mapping is present in SIEM (tenant.id, user.id, event.action, model_name).
- Pre-create a dashboard for pen-test telemetry: top 10 actions, failed auths, high-latency inference events, anomalous IPs.
- Set temporary rate-based alerts for unusual spikes during the engagement.
- Confirm retention policy for pen-test indexes (default 90 days unless longer required by legal).

Finding summary template (used by vendor):
- Finding ID: PT-<engagement>-<serial>
- Title (1-line)
- Affected assets (list)
- Severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low)
- Description (steps to reproduce, request/response excerpts – redacted)
- Supporting evidence refs (manifest entries, object paths)
- Suggested remediation (concrete steps)
- Responsible owner (redwood target team contact)
- Suggested verification steps and ETA estimate for fix
- CVSS or internal severity mapping if applicable

Remediation plan template (for internal tracking):
- Finding ID
- Root cause analysis (short)
- Action items (owner, ticket link, ETA, test criteria)
- Rollback plan (if remediation risks service impact)
- Verification plan: include automated queries against audit logs and SIEM alerts to confirm fix. Example verification query: event.action:role.assign AND outcome:success AND timestamp:[postfix] where postfix is after remediation window.
- Closure signoff: security owner + product owner + QA engineer.

Verification checklist (post-remediation):
- Re-run RBAC smoke tests using the original pen-tester test account and confirm denied write attempts.
- Re-export audit logs for the verification window and compare happenevents to baseline (diff manifests and checksums).
- Validate SIEM rule fires on test anomalies (simulate if safe).
- Update policy lint and snapshot role bindings.

Operational caveats / gotchas:
- Be explicit about clock skew. All timestamps must be normalized to UTC before ingestion to the SIEM.
- Avoid handing live credentials. Prefer temporary signed URLs or time-limited read-only credentials.
- If a vendor requests write-capability for an exploit test, require a separate sandbox environment; never grant write on prod.
- Limit test concurrency to avoid hitting autoscaling or quota systems that would affect customer traffic.

Appendix A: quick commands (placeholders - do not run without parameterizing)
- export-audit --start 2026-02-20T00:00:00Z --end 2026-02-22T23:59:59Z --filter "tags:pen-test" --format ndjson | gzip > siem-audit-20260220.ndjson.gz
- sha256sum siem-audit-20260220.ndjson.gz > siem-audit-20260220.sha256
- evidence-handoff --bucket redwood-evidence --prefix pt-12345 --expire 72h --allow-ips 203.0.113.0/24

Appendix B: minimal verification queries
- RBAC role binding check: SELECT * FROM role_bindings WHERE role='pen-tester-readonly' AND active=true;
- Failed write attempt detection: event.action:/write|delete/ AND outcome:failure AND timestamp:[start TO end]

Open questions to resolve before next engagement:
- Do we want permanent pen-test prefixes in the SIEM indices or temporary time-limited indexes?
- Policy for vendor-requested sandbox environments: who funds and who owns the sandbox?
- Retention beyond 90 days for legal evidence requests (legal has asked for 1 year in specific cases).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working draft. The automation commands reference internal helpers that live in infra/tools. Please suggest concrete command names if you prefer different flags or semantics.
- If you are going to be the on-call SRE for an upcoming engagement, add your name to the 'collaborators' list and ensure the ephemeral access play is validated in staging at least 72 hours prior to the start window.

End of document.
